title: Story of a Soul: The Autobiography of St. Thérèse of Lisieux
author: St. Thérèse of Lisieux (Marie-Françoise-Thérèse Martin)
edition_analyzed: Standard English translation (most widely accepted text for devotional and analytical use)
target_audience: Readers interested in the lives of saints
Spiritual seekers and those exploring Carmelite spirituality
Theologians and scholars of Christian mysticism
core_themes: Simplicity and the 'Little Way' of trust in God
The transformative power of love and sacrifice
Suffering as a path to spiritual growth
primary_purpose: To share Thérèse's intimate spiritual journey and her doctrine of the 'Little Way,' offering readers a powerful model of sanctity through simplicity, humility, and love for God. The book seeks to inspire ordinary believers to pursue holiness in everyday life.

structure_format.organization: Divided into three main manuscripts (letters/memoirs written for her religious superiors and sisters), often supplemented by poetry, prayers, and appendices in many editions
features: Detailed recollections of childhood, convent life, and spiritual insight
Direct addresses to Jesus and candid reflection on personal struggles

key_concepts_lessons: Holiness is accessible to all through small daily acts performed with great love.
Childlike spiritual trust and surrender are hallmarks of Thérèse’s 'Little Way.'
Great sanctity is not always found in grand gestures, but in humility and self-offering.
Suffering, accepted with love and patience, can become redemptive.
A simple, loving relationship with God is the essence of the Christian life.
The importance of hidden sacrifices and the value of being 'unknown and little.'
notable_features: Classic of modern Catholic literature and spirituality
Declared a Doctor of the Church in part due to these writings
cultural_historical_context: Written at the request of her superiors while Thérèse was a cloistered Carmelite nun in late 19th-century France. Published posthumously after her death at age 24 from tuberculosis, the autobiography became a spiritual classic that profoundly impacted Catholic spirituality, especially through its emphasis on humility and the accessibility of sanctity.
reception_impact: Considered a foundational work in modern Catholic spirituality
Inspired devotion to the 'Little Flower' worldwide
Credited with miracles and the rapid spread of Thérèse’s fame
Highly praised by popes and theologians for its deep spirituality in simple language
Non-Catholics have also found spiritual resonance in its message of radical love and trust
comparable_titles: The Interior Castle by St. Teresa of Avila
Autobiography of St. Teresa of Avila
The Way of Perfection by St. Teresa of Avila
Spiritual Childhood by Fr. Raymond de Thomas de Saint-Laurent
